instruction: Use FEniCS from the command line to optimize a 2D cantilever density field. Read /home/user/Desktop/problem_spec.json for the domain, design grid, solver mesh, material constants, boundary conditions, traction patch, density value bounds, and density design budget. Read /home/user/Desktop/baseline_density_field.csv as the initial feasible density field. You may use /home/user/Desktop/density_opt_base.py as the starter workflow. Create /home/user/Desktop/density_field.csv, /home/user/Desktop/solve_submission.py, and /home/user/Desktop/displacement.xdmf; if the XDMF writer creates a companion .h5 file, keep it in the same directory. The density CSV must be 10 by 20, all density values must be in [0, 1], and the density design budget requires mean density <= 0.40. Keep the domain, material constants, boundary conditions, traction patch, value bounds, and design budget from the problem specification unchanged.
